status_summary: DoDEA reviewed school libraries and curricula in early 2025 under the executive orders on gender ideology, the armed forces and K-12 schooling (EO 14168, EO 14185 and EO 14190); memos of 2025-02-05 described in a court opinion directed staff to move books on those topics out of student collections and to stop using listed curricular materials, and the opinion refers to more than 500 books removed. In E.K. v. DoDEA the Eastern District of Virginia on 2025-10-20 granted in part a preliminary injunction covering five schools and requiring removed materials to be restored there, denied systemwide relief, and on 2026-03-20 denied a motion to dismiss; cross-appeals were consolidated in the Fourth Circuit on 2026-01-02. EO 14191 (signed 2025-01-29) directed the Secretary of Defense to review ways for military families to use DOD funds at schools of their choice and to submit a plan within 90 days; a DOD news item of 2025-05-27 says that review was under way, and no plan or enacted savings account option was found. The health-policy part of the audit was not matched to any action.

timeline.event: EO 14191 signed: Secretary of Defense to review how military-connected families could use DOD funds for schools of their choice and submit a plan within 90 days.

DoDEA's acting chief academic officer issues memos directing that books potentially related to gender ideology or discriminatory equity ideology be moved out of student collections and that listed curricular materials no longer be used (as described in the court opinion).
Parents file E.K. v. DoDEA in the Eastern District of Virginia challenging the book removals and curricular changes.
DOD news item reports the Secretary of Defense ordered a review of support for homeschooling military-connected families, and a separate school-choice review under EO 14191.

Court grants in part a preliminary injunction covering five DoDEA schools, barring further removals under the orders there and requiring removed materials to be restored; relief for all DoDEA schools denied.
Fourth Circuit consolidates the government's appeal and the plaintiffs' cross-appeal (Nos. 25-2497 and 26-1002).
District court denies the government's motion to dismiss; a renewed motion to modify the injunction and a motion for an indicative ruling were pending as of the latest docket entry (2026-05-07).

The Clearinghouse district docket excerpt ends 2026-05-07 and the Justia Fourth Circuit docket ends 2026-06-08; it shows briefing (government opening brief filed 2026-03-27, plaintiffs' brief 2026-05-27, amicus briefs in early June 2026, reply due 2026-06-26), no argument date and no decision, but later activity was not checked.
